<reason>B made the decisive comparison clearer: some exclusivity revenue versus dependable live access, while preserving most paid marquee inventory. B directly answered the revenue and definition questions and honestly conceded possible financial losses. A established a plausible opportunity cost but never justified its claimed consequences for development and safety. It also repeatedly misrepresented free-to-air as requiring cable despite explicit corrections. Its answer on access offered paid passes or non-viewing substitutes without establishing comparable free live coverage.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B dismantled A’s funding-versus-access dichotomy: most marquee games remain monetisable, free broadcasters still pay rights fees, and losing some premium does not establish threatened development budgets. B then exposed why cheap passes, radio, text and highlights do not answer exclusion from live viewing.</best_rebuttal>
